definition: Qwen (also known as Tongyi Qianwen, Chinese: 通义千问; pinyin: Tōngyì Qiānwèn) is a family of predominantly open weights large and small language models (LLM and SLM) developed by Alibaba Cloud.
details: Its latest version, Qwen3.8; the 2.4 trillion parameter model was the second largest and second most powerful open weights LLM and Chinese LLM released by 12 August 2026, after Kimi K3. Larger models require a revenue sharing agreement from providers generating more than US$50 million annually. The distilled Qwen3.8 27B was released under a more permissive Apache License. The first iteration of Qwen, based on Meta AI's Llama 1, launched a beta in April 2023, releasing the weights of its 72B model that December. A local version of Qwen is used by Apple Intelligence in China, integrated with the operating system. Permissive licenses and smaller releases make them a common starting point for further fine-tuned and abliterated models in the open-source community.

explainer.lead: Qwen is a family of open-weight language models from Alibaba Cloud, spanning small to trillion-parameter scale. Permissive licenses and small releases make it a common base for fine-tuning in the open-source community.

tiers.eli5: It’s a family of AI chatbots made by Alibaba, some small enough to run locally and some huge, with the smaller versions often free to modify.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers fine-tune distilled Qwen models under permissive licenses for local use; a pitfall is that the largest models require a revenue-sharing agreement from providers earning over US$50 million annually.
tiers.paperLevel: A family of predominantly open-weight large and small language models developed by Alibaba Cloud; the latest version, Qwen3.8, includes a 2.4 trillion parameter model, while the distilled Qwen3.8 27B is released under an Apache License.

explainer.example: A developer fine-tunes the Qwen3.8 27B model, released under Apache License, for a local assistant, while a large provider earning over US$50 million annually must sign a revenue-sharing agreement to use the 2.4 trillion parameter model.
